title: UK AISI finds attack-policy choice can make AI monitor evaluations misleading
summary: Two evaluator items and no new vulnerability, incident or capability item. UK AISI reported that the miss rate of a GPT-5.4-based agent monitor ranged from about 0.2% to 23% depending on how synthetic attacks were generated, and METR analyzed an apparent acceleration in OpenAI's pretraining loss improvement since early 2026.

items.title: METR flags a sharp speed-up in pretraining loss improvement
items.summary: METR authors analyze OpenAI's published base-model log-perplexity for 13 models and say it has been falling about seven times faster since early 2026 than in 2022-2025 (roughly 0.156 per year versus 0.022). They lay out three views on whether this should change capability forecasts, state there is no consensus, and ask all developers to publish pretraining loss on fixed held-out data.
items.products: OpenAI base models since GPT-3.5 (pretraining log-perplexity)
items.note: Forecasting analysis, not a safety evaluation result.

items.title: UK AISI: choice of attack policy can make monitor evaluations misleading
items.summary: AISI's Red Team tested an ex-production GPT-5.4-based monitor watching a Qwen agent and found the miss rate depends heavily on how synthetic attacks are generated: about 0.2% with basic prompting versus 23% with transcript editing at top optimisation. It concludes a low miss rate under one attack policy can give false confidence and that synthetic evaluations alone cannot assure deployment monitoring.
items.note: Accompanied by a paper per the post.
